description:
🎬 Try invideo Editor: https://invideo.io/?ref=gakul&via=influencer

💻 My PowerGrade: https://shop.gakuyen.com/products/odyssey-powergrade

🎨 Try My LUTs: https://shop.gakuyen.com/products/ultimate-lut-pack

💽 Color Grade with my Plugin: https://shop.gakuyen.com/products/genesis-plugin

📖 My Masterclass: https://shop.gakuyen.com/products/the-complete-collection-masterclass-bundle  

In this video I’m breaking down a different way I’ve been approaching the beginning of my editing workflow - going from a large amount of raw footage to selects, a first cut, sound design and effects, and eventually into Premiere Pro for my usual finishing workflow.
I tested invideo Editor with my own footage to see how much of the repetitive part of an edit I could get through before moving into the more detailed creative decisions. I go through how I imported and organized the footage, found selects, started building the timeline, added sound design and effects, and then continued refining the project from there.

For me, the interesting part isn’t having a tool make the entire video. It’s being able to get through some of the repetitive work faster while still having an editable timeline that I can go in and change myself.
